# 1 Clement Chapter 50 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 50 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_050_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 50

**50:1** How blessed and wonderful are the gifts of God, dear friends!

**50:2** Life that never ends; radiant righteousness; truth spoken boldly; faith that gives real confidence; self-control lived out in holiness — and all of this is within our reach.

**50:3** But what of the things God has prepared for those who wait for him? Only the Creator and Father of the ages — the All-Holy One — truly knows how great and beautiful those things are.

**50:4** So let us do everything we can to be counted among those who wait for him, so that we may share in the gifts he has promised.

**50:5** How do we get there? By keeping our minds faithfully fixed on God. By seeking what is pleasing and acceptable to him. By doing what aligns with his perfect will. By walking in the way of truth and stripping off everything contrary to it — unrighteousness, lawlessness, greed, strife, malice, deceit, gossip, slander, hatred of God, arrogance, boasting, empty vanity, and coldness toward strangers.

**50:6** People who live that way are hateful to God — and not just those who do it, but those who applaud it too.

**50:7** For Scripture says: "But to the wicked person God said: Why do you recite my laws and speak of my covenant with your mouth?

**50:8** You hated discipline and threw my words away. When you saw a thief, you sided with him; you made yourself at home with adulterers.

**50:9** Your mouth poured out evil; your tongue constructed lies. You sat there talking against your brother, spreading slander against your own mother's child.

**50:10** You did all this and I stayed silent — and you thought, you lawless one, that I was just like you. But I will confront you and lay the charges out in front of you.

**50:11** Take this to heart, you who forget God, or he will come for you like a lion and no one will be there to rescue you.

**50:12** Grateful praise is the sacrifice that honors me — and that is the path by which I will show you God's salvation."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the spirit of Clement's pastoral appeal.*
